claims.text: Sputtering the alloy as a 100 nm film introduces the thin-film geometry proposed as the controlled intervention.
The sputtered film retains a first-order magnetostructural transition.
The magnetocaloric response is maintained through the first-order magnetostructural transition in the film.
Under cycles up to 2 T over 250–350 K, the thin-film intervention produces a 40% increase in cooling power relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Under cycles up to 2 T over 250–350 K, the thin-film intervention produces a 20% reduction in hysteresis losses relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The cooling-power and hysteresis benefits become more pronounced at higher cooling rates.
The predictions hold for film thicknesses from 50 to 200 nm.
The predictions hold only when interface quality does not significantly degrade the magnetocaloric response.
The magnitudes of the cooling-power increase and hysteresis-loss reduction depend on film thickness and interface quality.

contradictions.description: The intervention is production of a sputtered thin film, but the comparator is only called the as-deposited alloy. A sputtered film is itself normally an as-deposited state, so the intervention and baseline are not operationally distinguished by geometry, thickness, or processing history.
